conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good afternoon, Mr. ___ . I'm Dr. ___ . You're here today to start high-dose Cytoxan as part of your stem cell mobilization for multiple myeloma.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that’s right. I’ve been doing well on Revlimid and dexamethasone, so I’m ready for this next step.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great to hear. Before we start chemo, we always do a quick check-up and some labs, including a urinalysis, to make sure everything is stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Makes sense. I’ve had a lot of tests lately with all the transplant prep.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We got your urine results back, and there’s something we need to address before starting chemotherapy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh? Is something wrong?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The test shows signs of a urinary tract infection — nitrites were positive and there were a lot of white blood cells. But I notice you’re not having symptoms like burning or urgency.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, I haven’t felt any of that. My urine seems normal. Could it be a mistake?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s not a mistake. The sample wasn’t contaminated — very few epithelial cells — so this looks like a real, though asymptomatic, infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Asymptomatic? So I don’t feel sick, but I still need treatment?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. With your medical history and the fact that we’re about to suppress your immune system with high-dose chemo, even a silent infection needs to be treated first.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I see. So we’re not doing the Cytoxan today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, we’re holding off on chemotherapy for now. Safety first. We’ll send you home with an antibiotic — levofloxacin — for one week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that makes sense. Is levofloxacin safe with my other meds, like Coumadin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good question. We’ve checked — it’s safe to use briefly. We’ll monitor you, but it’s a standard choice for UTIs like this.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One more thing — the urine culture came back showing mixed bacterial flora, which suggests possible contamination, but given the initial urinalysis, we’re still treating the infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So was it a false positive?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not necessarily. The urinalysis was clear for infection signs, and we don’t want to take risks before transplant. Better to treat and reschedule chemo.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re cleared to go home. Take the levofloxacin once daily for seven days. We’ll reschedule your chemotherapy after you’ve completed the course.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And my leg swelling — should I be worried about that too?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your exam shows mild bilateral edema, but your heart function is normal and you’re not short of breath. We’ll keep an eye on it, but it’s not a concern for today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my citalopram? Psychiatry had me on it for depression, but I heard it might be stopped before transplant.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, the plan is to discontinue it before transplant, as discussed. We’ll coordinate that with your psychiatrist.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Alright, thank you. I’ll take the antibiotic and wait for the next chemo appointment.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Call us if you develop fever, pain, or any new symptoms. Otherwise, we’ll be in touch soon to reschedule.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just confirming — you’ve received discharge instructions and your prescription for levofloxacin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I have everything. I’ll take it as directed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing the right thing by taking care of this infection first. Stay well, and we’ll see you soon for the next steps.
